note: Ground truth authored by the overseer via sutra + reads. semantic_strength: strong = the concept is not named in code in any word-form; weak = the naive symptom keyword is absent but the feature/identifier names the concept.

FL1.mechanism: Scheduler tick -> enqueue_events_for_all_sites -> enqueue_events_for_site -> enqueue_events iterates Scheduled Job Type docs (filtered stopped=0) -> ScheduledJobType.enqueue, which enqueues an RQ job only if is_event_due() and not is_job_in_queue().
must_contain: at least ONE silent-skip point: is_scheduler_inactive (maintenance/pause_scheduler) OR schedule_jobs_based_on_activity dormant-site skip OR stopped=0 filter OR is_job_in_queue dedup (logged only) OR bad-cron caught+logged

FL2.mechanism: Document.has_permission returns True immediately if self.flags.ignore_permissions is truthy, else delegates to frappe.permissions.has_permission (role perms + user/share/owner perms).
must_contain: frappe/permissions.py has_permission as the real check

FL3.mechanism: @rate_limit decorator wraps an endpoint; RateLimiter tracks a per-key request count in redis within a window; over the limit it raises/responds 429.
must_contain: redis-backed counter within a time window

FS1.mechanism: On update, check_if_latest compares the in-memory `modified` timestamp against the DB `modified`; if they differ the doc was changed after it was read, and it raises frappe.TimestampMismatchError ('Document has been modified after you have opened it').
must_contain: raises TimestampMismatchError (or frappe conflict error) on mismatch

FS2.mechanism: Jobs are routed to named queues short/default/long (enqueue(queue=...)); each has its own timeout and its own worker(s), so a flood of long jobs sits on the long queue and does not block short-queue workers. Additionally at_front_when_starved inserts LIFO when a queue looks starved.
must_contain: separate short/default/long queues so slow jobs don't block fast ones

FS3.mechanism: Every cache key is prefixed by the site's db_name in make_key (unless shared=True), so keys are namespaced per site; a worker serving many sites can't read site A's cached value during a site B request because the key includes the site's db_name.
must_contain: make_key prefixes cache keys with the site db_name
per-site key namespacing prevents cross-site reads

DL1.mechanism: run() calls the rerank model, filters results by score >= score_threshold (drops below-threshold), sorts descending, and truncates to top_n.

DL2.mechanism: Before running a model call, QuotaService.reserve/consume reserves billing quota via BillingService; if exceeded it raises QuotaExceededError (surfaced as InvokeRateLimitError), blocking the call.
must_contain: QuotaService reserve/consume before the model call

DL3.mechanism: {{#node.field#}} refs are matched by the variable pattern and resolved by VariablePool.convert_template, which now lives in the external graphon dependency (not vendored). Unresolved refs are kept as raw selector text / raise 'variable not found' at some call sites.
must_contain: the resolver lives in the external graphon package (not in the repo)

DS1.mechanism: Per-app (client_id) max_active_requests: RateLimit.enter checks the Redis hash length (hlen) of active requests; if >= max_active_requests it raises AppInvokeQuotaExceededError; exit hdel decrements; RateLimitGenerator.close releases on stream end.
must_contain: per-app active-request cap via RateLimit.enter (Redis hlen vs max_active_requests)

DS2.mechanism: AppQueueManager.listen polls with a timeout bounded by APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME; once elapsed time exceeds it, it force-publishes a QueueStopEvent (stopped_by USER_MANUAL) regardless of whether generation finished, truncating the run.
must_contain: APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME elapsed -> force QueueStopEvent in the queue manager
the stop is emitted as an event (QueueStopEvent) that ends the run

DS3.mechanism: On an indexing exception, _handle_indexing_error sets the document's indexing_status to 'error' (with the error + stopped_at), so it ends up visibly failed. Re-indexing is user-triggered via retry_document_indexing_task, which guards against concurrent/double retries (raises ValueError if already retrying) rather than auto-retrying endlessly.
must_contain: retries are user-triggered/guarded, not endless auto-retry
